result.summary: This PR adds an optional sat_vb boolean argument to getmempoolinfo, getnetworkinfo, estimatesmartfee, and estimaterawfee so their feerate fields can be printed in sat/vB instead of the default BTC/kvB. It introduces a new ValueFromFeeRate helper in core_io alongside the existing ValueFromAmount, with unit tests, and keeps BTC/kvB as the unconditional default for backwards compatibility. It is explicitly framed by the author as a proof-of-concept for the broader sat/vb migration discussed in issue #32093.
result.problem: RPC callers and downstream software (wallets, explorers, Lightning implementations) currently receive feerates only in BTC/kvB, a unit the author and several reviewers agree is awkward compared to the widely used sat/vB, forcing every consumer to do their own conversion.

open_concerns: glozow argued a hidden default-toggle could be dangerous if the default were ever changed later (a factor-of-100000 unit surprise), preferring separate differently-named fields instead; author responded that the default will not change and kept the boolean-arg design, and no further pushback followed.
w0xlt pointed out a real bug where estimaterawfee only converted the top-level feerate but left bucket startrange/endrange in sat/kvB units; author incorporated w0xlt's fix with co-authorship.
resolved_concerns: maflcko's concerns about hardcoded defaults and floating point for monetary values were addressed by moving to self.Arg<bool> and a fixed-point ValueFromFeeRate helper.
w0xlt's concern about UniValue leaking into policy/feerate.h was addressed by moving the helper into core_io instead.
musaHaruna's stylistic suggestion about signed/unsigned arithmetic was declined by the author with a stated rationale (readability), and musaHaruna did not push back.

categories.name: rpc
categories.evidence: Adds a new optional argument to getmempoolinfo, getnetworkinfo, estimatesmartfee, and estimaterawfee and a new core_io helper used by RPC output formatting; carries the RPC/REST/ZMQ label.
categories.rationale: P3 because it is a real, backwards-compatible usability improvement addressing a pain point named in issue #32093 ('Returning feerates in BTC/kvB it can be very burdensome'), but no external consumer is cited as blocked on it and it changes no compatibility-critical existing output by default. It has some leverage as a stated proof-of-concept for a larger unit-migration effort, but that effort's shape is still being debated (glozow's alternative field-based design).

uncertainties: Whether the boolean-toggle-per-RPC design or glozow's alternative (separate named fields, e.g. feerate_satvb) will ultimately be the accepted approach for the broader #32093 migration is still open; this affects whether this PR's specific mechanism survives long-term even though the underlying goal is uncontested.

No maintainer with strong authority on RPC compatibility policy (e.g. one of the RPC leads) has weighed in beyond maflcko's initial code-level comments, so full project buy-in on this exact mechanism is not fully established.
result.card: This PR adds an optional sat_vb boolean argument to getmempoolinfo, getnetworkinfo, estimatesmartfee, and estimaterawfee so their feerate output can be shown in sat/vB instead of the long-standing BTC/kvB, addressing a usability pain point tracked in issue #32093 for RPC callers and downstream software that currently must convert units themselves. The author frames it as backwards-compatible proof-of-concept, and reviewer glozow raised a substantive but ultimately unresurfaced concern that a hidden default toggle could be dangerous if the default were ever flipped later, suggesting separate named fields instead; the author held the current design and no pushback followed. w0xlt found and the author fixed a real bug where estimaterawfee's bucket ranges stayed in the old unit while the top-level feerate switched. The PR now has concept ACKs from w0xlt, musaHaruna, and jonatack and one code ACK, with the author actively pushing as recently as 2026-09-10 and nothing known pending that would invalidate a review. It has no dependencies on other open PRs and no one else's work is blocked on it, making it a worthwhile but deferrable RPC usability improvement rather than a critical one.
